Frontend Analytics page wired into App.js (/app/analytics) + Layout sidebar (data-testid nav-analytics-link present for owner). UI verified end-to-end: Overview live banner (in_progress=12, completed=0, revenue $0, new_finance_apps=19, funded=1) + 8 KPI cards (Revenue $2,200 / Jobs completed 1 / Avg ticket $2,200 / Active customers 3 / Finance funded $5,000 / Finance count 1 / Jobs total 34 / Jobs paid 1) + Revenue AreaChart renders. Date filter re-renders without crash.
critical_code_review_comments: Analytics.jsx line 92 ternary: `tab === 'techs' ? 'technicians' : tab === 'memberships' ? null : tab === 'overview' ? null : tab` is hard to follow. The `.includes(...)` then checks if null/string is in the array. It works (null/overview/memberships exclude correctly) but a simple set like `['revenue','techs','marketing','financing','leaderboard'].includes(tab)` would be clearer.

Analytics.jsx Overview useEffect re-creates the 30s polling interval on every params change (deps=[JSON.stringify(params)]). Each date-filter change tears down + sets a new interval — fine but consider a separate effect for the polling tick so the interval only depends on auth/user, not date filter.

Analytics.jsx Memberships() does not respect branch_id or date range filters even though those filters render in the global header. Backend membership endpoint also ignores branch_id. Either grey out the filter when on Memberships tab or document that memberships are tenant-wide.

analytics.py overview/revenue/etc use string-comparison for date ranges ($gte/$lte on created_at as ISO strings). This works because Python isoformat is lexicographically sortable, BUT mixing tz-aware and tz-naive ISO strings in the DB could mis-sort. Suggest standardising created_at writes to always include +00:00.
analytics.py membership_retention does NOT accept branch_id — inconsistent with other endpoints. Fine if memberships are company-level but UI should hide the branch filter on that tab.

analytics.py export_csv financing branch: writes by_status dict keys (started/decisioned/signed/funded/declined) as separate rows but the funnel computation already aggregated. The CSV is the 'status breakdown' not the funnel — fine but not labelled in CSV header.
analytics.py revenue_series default_days=60 but overview uses 30 — slight inconsistency in 'default window' across endpoints. Frontend always passes explicit start/end so not user-facing.

All key UI elements have data-testid attributes (analytics-tab-*, analytics-export-btn, analytics-start, analytics-end, analytics-branch, rev-gran-*, lb-metric-*, lb-row-*, tech-row-*, realtime-banner, calls-funnel, fin-funnel) — excellent testability.
